verdict.rationale: First-party docs list a TypeScript web library, Swift async sequences for iOS, and Kotlin FFI bindings, so a Kotlin route to Android exists. A community production report shows browser and mobile clients publishing to one relay, and the docs say the WebSocket fallback is automatic in every client. Android is never named explicitly, and Kotlin ships as FFI bindings rather than a native SDK. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented Android SDK, documentation that the session and track model is identical across web, iOS and Android, and hands-on corroboration of Android parity.

support.subject: As a developer, official client SDKs cover web, iOS, and Android with the same session and track model, so one backend serves every platform

citations.quote: Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
Async sequences for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS.
Browser, desktop, mobile and device clients publish Opus to one relay
The fallback is automatic in every client
